topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 Minute)
lecture_lines: A basis is like a coordinate system.
Any vector is a linear combination.
How do we describe this change?
animations: Fade in a Light Blue (#87CEFA) Dot at B2 with scale_factor=0.5.
Fade in a White (#FFFFFF) set of basis vectors, labeled i and j, layered over a.
Fade in a vector v as a linear combination of i and j.
Draw a new, rotated basis, labeled i' and j', in light green (#90EE90) on the.
Place the origin_group in area B2 to C4 with scale_factor=0.8.

sections.title: The Mechanism of Coordinate Transformation (1.5 Minutes)
lecture_lines: We map old to new coordinates.
P columns are new basis vectors.
Robot dogs use P to navigate.
Matrix P translates local steps globally.
animations: Display text 'v_new = P v_old' in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight matrix P in yellow (#FFFF00) and place at B4 with scale_factor=0.7.
Animate columns of P transforming into the basis vectors i' and j'.
Display the 'vec' vector at grid C5 with scale_factor=0.9.
Display a text box 'Robot Navigator' in light blue (#87CEFA) with and place grid at A3-F6 with scale_factor=0.4.

sections.title: The Change-of-Basis Formula (1.5 Minutes)
lecture_lines: Formula: v_B equals P inverse v_A.
A camera lens frame is new.
animations: Display formula 'v_B = P^{-1} v_A' in A4-C6 with scale_factor=0.75.
Highlight matrix P in orange (#FFA500) and its inverse P^{-1} in light blue (#87CEFA).
Animate the transformation of a point using with arrow at D5, scale_factor=0.8.
Show a camera viewport mapping to world with grid_group at A2-F6, scale_factor=0.9.
Flash the equality sign in bold green (#32CD32).
